flashcard_questions.q: What is an element in chemistry?
flashcard_questions.a: A substance made up of only one type of atom.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a compound in chemistry?
flashcard_questions.a: A substance formed when two or more elements are chemically bonded together.

flashcard_questions.q: What distinguishes a mixture from a compound?
flashcard_questions.a: The substances in a mixture are not chemically bonded together.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the relative charge of a proton?
What is the relative mass of an electron?
Why does an atom have no overall electrical charge?
flashcard_questions.a: It has equal numbers of protons and electrons.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the approximate radius of an atom?
Which number defines which element an atom belongs to?
flashcard_questions.a: The atomic number, the number of protons.

flashcard_questions.q: Sodium has mass number 23 and atomic number 11. How many neutrons does it have?
Who proposed the plum pudding model of the atom?
What did most alpha particles passing straight through the gold foil show?
flashcard_questions.a: The atom is mostly empty space.

flashcard_questions.q: What did the alpha particles that bounced back from the gold foil show?
flashcard_questions.a: The atom has a small dense nucleus with a positive charge.

flashcard_questions.q: How many electrons can the first shell of an atom hold?
What is the electronic structure of sodium, which has 11 electrons?

notes: 15 cards: 3 term→definition (element, compound, mixture), 3 value-and-unit (proton charge, electron mass, atomic radius), 2 person→discovery (Thomson, Chadwick), 2 experiment→conclusion from alpha scattering, 3 structure/calculation (atomic number, neutron count, shell capacity), 1 worked electronic structure, 1 causal (neutral atom). Dropped the separation techniques (filtration, chromatography) as they belong to the separations lesson, and dropped relative atomic mass weighted-mean detail as calculation rather than recall.
